data.title: US judge approves Getty Images bankruptcy loan over shareholder objections
data.description:
By Dietrich Knauth

A US bankruptcy judge on Monday approved a $143 million bankruptcy loan for Getty Images provided by Koch Equity Development, overruling objections from shareholders who had argued that the loan would allow Getty insiders to shortchange minority investors.

  • US Bankruptcy Judge J. Kate Stickles in Delaware said the loan was the best available financing for Getty's bankruptcy restructuring

  • Objecting shareholders had said the loan would essentially hand the company to the Getty family and Koch Equity Development while leaving other shareholders with nothing

  • Stickles on Friday denied shareholders' request for a court-appointed committee to represent equity holders

  • Getty cited court losses in investor litigation, its $1.46 billion ​in debt, a failed merger with Shutterstock, and increased competition from AI-generated imagery as reasons for its bankruptcy filing in October

  • Getty said affiliates of ​the Getty family and Koch Equity Development, which committed to ​provide up to $533 million in new equity, will own 100% of the company after the bankruptcy restructuring

  • Getty Images expects to complete ​the restructuring by ​year-end

The case is Getty Images Holdings Inc, ​US Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware, No. 26-11643

For Getty Images: Brian Schartz of Simpson Thacher & Bartlett

For an ad hoc group of equity holders: Shari Dwoskin and Robert Stark of ​Brown Rudnick

Read more:

Getty Images plans bankruptcy filing, to go private

Getty Images scraps $3.7 billion merger with Shutterstock over UK scrutiny

Getty Images says investor litigation helped push it to bankruptcy

data.title: UN food agency chief warns wars jeopardize food aid for 7.3 million more people
data.description:
Key points:
  • WFP chief calls for new Black Sea initiative
  • UN agency aims to feed 91 million people in 2027
  • Wars, attacks are raising transport costs, keeping grain from markets

By Andrea Shalal

World Food Programme Executive Director Luke Lindberg warned on Monday that shipping chokepoints linked to wars in the Middle East and Ukraine could raise the agency's costs by $727 million by mid-2027, threatening food aid for 7.3 million more people.

Lindberg, whom US President Donald Trump nominated and the United Nations appointed in September to head the world's largest humanitarian agency, called for new efforts to safeguard humanitarian shipments of Ukrainian and Russian grain through the Black Sea, modeled on a UN-brokered initiative that was in effect from 2022 to 2023.

Lindberg told the UN Security Council that constraints on food exports and farming inputs passing through the Strait of Hormuz, the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and the Black Sea were compounded by climate shocks like El Nino.

"It's an unthinkable scenario, and it could not come at a worse time," said Lindberg, a former US agriculture official, urging diplomats to focus on trying to find rapid solutions to ensure some 10 million tons of Ukrainian and Russian grain that were already in silos reached people in need.

He said 266 million people globally were already suffering from acute hunger and there was a risk of famine in parts of Sudan, South Sudan, and Somalia.

Lindberg told Reuters in an interview that it was critical to resolve the situation in the Black Sea, one of the world's breadbasket regions whose grains were vital to countries like Somalia and Yemen, which imports 90% of its food.

He urged diplomats to work on a humanitarian corridor similar to the Black Sea Grain Initiative, a UN-brokered deal agreed in ​July 2022 ​that allowed ⁠the safe export of nearly 33 million metric tons of ​Ukrainian grain. Russia withdrew from the agreement in 2023, complaining that its own ⁠food ​and fertilizer exports faced ​serious obstacles.

'UNTENABLE'

Lindberg told Reuters that any revived agreement would have to cover both Russian and Ukrainian exports to win agreement.

"It's untenable to have full grain silos in Ukraine and Poland and the region, and then you have empty stomachs in other parts of the world ... If a diplomatic solution can be reached, we stand ready to move grain from both Russia and Ukraine," he said.

The WFP head added Black Sea food shipments were down sharply this year, with 63% fewer wheat and maize vessels moving through the Bosphorus as of mid-October than at the same point in 2025. Over 300 attacks had been recorded and at least 40 crew members had been killed, he said.

That meant some 10 million tons of Russian and Ukrainian wheat might not reach global markets this year — enough to feed 44 million people, he said.

The food price index of the UN's Food and Agriculture Organization had hit a near four-year high this September, wheat prices were up almost 10% from January, and higher energy and transport costs had increased grocery prices, especially in import-dependent and food-insecure countries, Lindberg said.

Food yields will likely also be lower next season, given constraints in global fertilizer supplies, of which 30% flow through the Strait of Hormuz, he added.

The wars were taking a direct toll on WFP's humanitarian operations and sharply increasing its costs, he said. The WFP has already lowered its target to provide food assistance to 91 million people in 2027 from 110 million people this year, but higher costs could drive that number even lower, he said.

The agency's total costs last year were nearly $12.2 billion, so $727 million in additional costs by mid-2027 would mark an increase of nearly 6%. That number could rise further unless current conditions changed, the agency said.

data.title: Meta pauses Class C share issuance amid shareholder lawsuit
data.description:
Meta Platforms said on Monday it will not issue its planned Class C shares while it faces shareholder litigation challenging the company's proposed recapitalization, delaying a share sale program intended to help fund its artificial intelligence investments.

  • The social media giant agreed not to issue the shares during the pre-trial and trial proceedings in the lawsuit brought by shareholders in Delaware's Court of Chancery. The trial is scheduled to begin on April 19, 2027

  • The shareholder litigation challenges Meta's plan to create a new class of non-voting Class C common stock in January 2027

  • The structure would effectively result in a two-for-one split and is designed to give Meta flexibility to fund acquisitions and retain top talent while maintaining CEO Mark Zuckerberg's voting control

  • The delay also affects Meta's planned $60 billion at-the-market stock sale program, which is not expected to begin until the Class C shares start trading

  • The company has been investing heavily in advanced chips and data centers as it steps up competition with AI leaders OpenAI and Anthropic, while positioning itself at the forefront of the emerging consumer AI agent race

data.title: This Space ETF Breaks Past Its Seven-Day Decline Amid NASA’s Partnership Call For Moon Nuclear Reactor
data.description:
Key points:
  • NASA opened bidding for Lunar Reactor-1 (LR-1), a 20-kilowatt fission system designed to launch by 2030 and supply continuous electricity across the Moon for at least five years. 
  • Proposals are due December 21 under a framework co-managed with the Department of Energy.
  • The Tema Space Innovators ETF (NASA) rose about 8%, ending its seven consecutive session losing streak. 

NASA on Monday opened bidding for private industry partners to design, test, and construct the first nuclear fission power plant intended for the lunar surface, targeting a launch-ready system by 2030.

While the federal space agency doubles down on atomic energy for deep space, the announcement lands during a turbulent stretch on Wall Street for commercial nuclear startups and space-sector equities.

However, major nuclear power stocks, including Oklo (OKLO) and NuScale Power (SMR) gained about 5.6% on Monday, while lunar robotics firm Intuitive Machines (LUNR) and rocket launch service provider Rocket Lab (RKLB) added between 12% and 9.5% each.

The Tema Space Innovators ETF (NASA) surged about 8% on Monday, breaking free from seven consecutive days of decline following the announcement.

Powering Through The Lunar Night

Dubbed Lunar Reactor-1, or LR-1, the proposed fission system is engineered to generate 20 kilowatts of electrical power, which is roughly equivalent to the annual energy consumption of 16 average U.S. households.

Once deployed on the Moon, the unit is expected to operate continuously for a minimum of five years, supplying electricity to future astronaut habitats, communications arrays, surface rovers and scientific payloads.

“A reliable source of safe and abundant energy will be vital to future exploration of the lunar and Martian surface,” said Brian Giblin, NASA’s Lunar Reactor-1 program manager.

Unlike solar panels, which rely on uninterrupted sunlight, nuclear fission provides steady baseload power regardless of environmental conditions, NASA said in a press release. That capability is critical on the Moon, where a single lunar night lasts roughly 14 Earth days, as well as in permanently shadowed craters near the lunar poles believed to harbor water ice.

Nuclear And Space Stocks Remain Under Pressure

NASA's renewed commitment to space-based fission arrives as terrestrial advanced nuclear developers face intense market skepticism pertaining to balance sheet health and timely licensing.

Shares of advanced fission developer OKLO have tumbled roughly 73% year to date amid investor concerns over licensing timelines and pre-revenue cash burn, despite recently securing operational clearance from the Department of Energy for its Groves-1 test reactor.

Meanwhile, small modular reactor maker NuScale Power (SMR) has shed nearly 77% of its value so far in 2026.

Lunar lander specialist Intuitive Machines Inc. (LUNR) is down roughly 25% year-to-date, while launch provider Rocket Lab USA Inc. (RKLB) dropped about 25% so far this year.

NASA Stock: Retail View 

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits was ‘extremely bullish’ with ‘high’ message volumes.

NASA stock has lost about 26% year-to-date.

data.title: Soybean, corn barge bids mixed as supplies of empty barges tighten
data.description:
Basis bids for soybeans shipped by barge to US Gulf Coast export terminals were mixed on Monday for nearby months, while basis offers for corn were steady to mixed, traders said.

  • Rates for empty barges firmed on the Mississippi River in St. Louis, Missouri, and at points along the Ohio River, as demand for barges firmed and supplies tightened, one dealer said.

  • The USDA said on Monday exporters sold 110,000 metric tons of white wheat to unknown destinations for delivery in the 2026/2027 marketing year.

  • Separately, the USDA also reported on Monday export inspections for the week ended November 19 of 1,555,054 metric tons of US soybeans, which was within trade expectations.

  • USDA reported weekly export inspections of 1,190,786 tons of US corn, above trade expectations.

  • Meanwhile, France reported an outbreak of highly pathogenic H5N1 bird flu in the northern part of the country, the World Organisation for Animal Health said on Monday, as Europe faces a seasonal rise in the deadly disease.

  • CIF soybean barge bids were mixed, with prices slightly pressured in nearby months and firming in deferred months.

  • CIF soybean barges loaded in November were bid at 106 cents a bushel over Chicago Board of Trade January futures , while December loadings were steady — bid at 110 cents over January futures. Meanwhile, bids for January loadings were at 115 cents over futures and soybean barges loaded in February were bid at 106 cents over March futures , both up 1 cent.

  • FOB basis offers for soybeans loaded in November were unquoted, while December loadings were offered at 121 cents over January futures.

  • CIF corn barges loaded in November eased, with bids at 84 cents over December corn futures, while bids for December loadings were steady at 94 cents over futures. Deferred months were mixed.

  • FOB basis offers for corn loaded in November were offered at 106 cents over December futures, while December loadings were offered at 110 cents over futures.

data.title: Coca-Cola CFO John Murphy to Retire in 2027
data.description:
By Josh Beckerman

Coca-Cola Chief Financial Officer John Murphy, who joined the company in 1988 and became CFO in 2019, plans to retire in 2027.

Bristol Myers Squibb CFO David Elkins will become Coca-Cola CFO on April 2. Murphy will remain president and retire later in the year.

Bristol Myers Squibb said Kevin Dillon, head of corporate finance and business operations, will become CFO on March 1. The company also reaffirmed 2026 guidance.

Murphy's earlier roles at Coca-Cola have included president of the Asia Pacific and president of the South Latin unit. Before joining Coca‑Cola, Murphy was an auditor at Price Waterhouse.

Vertical Data, through its Swedish subsidiary, sold 95% of Cirenso and certain related loans to a buyer owned by a joint venture of Fund affiliates and Vertical Edge. The Contract Note provides for SEK 54.3 million in aggregate purchase consideration, including a previously advanced deposit; the cash purchase price paid at closing was SEK 45.7 million. Vertical Data retained a 5% stake in Cirenso, while a separate loan transfer agreement restructured additional loan claims connected with the transaction.

Agreement 1: Vertical Data Sells 95% of Cirenso and Related Loans for SEK 54.3 Million

  • Agreement type: Share and loan sale under Contract Note
  • Counterparty: Swedish Buyer owned by Sweden JV affiliates
  • Signed / Effective: Nov 16 2026 / Nov 16 2026
  • Duration / Termination: Completed at closing
  • Reason: Sell a majority stake in Cirenso while retaining a minority interest

Agreement 2: Vertical Data Transfers SEK 4.1 Million Cirenso-Related Loan Claims

  • Agreement type: Loan Transfer Agreement
  • Counterparty: Buyer, Cirenso, Vertical Edge and Fund affiliates
  • Signed / Effective: Nov 16 2026 / Nov 16 2026
  • Duration / Termination: Not specified
  • Reason: Reallocate loan claims as part of the Cirenso sale

Original SEC Filing: Vertical Data Inc. [ VDTA ] - 8-K - Nov. 23, 2026

data.title: Hawthorn Bancshares amends CEO Brent Giles’s employment agreement, raises base salary
data.description:
Hawthorn Bancshares amended and restated CEO Brent Giles’s employment agreement, raising his minimum annual base salary to $500,000 and revising his severance and other terms.

IndividualBrent Giles
RoleChief Executive Officer of Hawthorn Bancshares and Hawthorn Bank
Type of ChangeAmended and restated employment agreement
Effective DateNovember 19, 2026; salary increase effective January 1, 2026
Agreement TermInitial two-year term, automatically extending annually to maintain a rolling two-year term; either side may give at least 90 days’ notice of non-renewal
Compensation/Agreement TermsMinimum annual base salary increased from $450,000 to $500,000. Eligible for a target annual incentive bonus of 35% and maximum of 52% of base salary, plus RSU awards targeted at up to 50% of base salary, subject to Board-set vesting conditions.
BenefitsAnnual executive health examination reimbursement of up to $10,000 replaces country club dues benefit.
SeveranceWithout-cause termination or resignation for good reason: two times base salary plus target annual short-term incentive, prorated target incentive for the termination year, and up to 18 monthly COBRA premium payments.
Change-in-Control TermsQualifying termination during the protection period: lump sum of 2.99 times base salary plus target annual short-term incentive, reduced by severance already paid; subject to agreement conditions and regulatory limits.
Other TermsNon-compete and non-solicitation covenants apply for 18 months after employment ends. Incentive compensation is subject to applicable clawback policies; no tax gross-up is provided.

Original SEC Filing: HAWTHORN BANCSHARES, INC. [ HWBK ] - 8-K - Nov. 23, 2026

data.title: Frontier Nuclear receives Nasdaq non-compliance notice over late annual filing
data.description:
Key points:

  • Frontier Nuclear and Minerals received a Nasdaq notice on November 18, 2026, for failing to timely file its FY2026 Annual Report.

  • Nasdaq has given Frontier until January 18, 2027, to submit a plan to regain compliance.

  • The company expects to file its annual report before the deadline and will submit a compliance plan if required.

  • If Nasdaq accepts the plan, Frontier could receive an extension of up to 180 days, through May 17, 2027, to regain compliance.

data.title: Wall Street soars on Huang's return to Nvidia, Treasury yields rise
data.description:
Key points:
  • Nvidia shares surge 31% on Jensen Huang's return
  • Dollar index hits 19-month high with bets on a hawkish Fed
  • Tech shares lead indexes higher, S&P gains 4.7%

By Sabrina Valle

US stocks soared on Monday after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive following pressure from US President Donald Trump. Shorter-dated US Treasury yields climbed and the dollar rose as traders bet on a more hawkish Federal Reserve.

The company's decision sparked a sharp reversal of last week's global equity market rout, triggered in part by the leadership crisis at the chipmaker. Nvidia shares surged as much as 36% before closing 31% higher, driving a broad rally across chip-related and technology stocks on Wall Street.

The Nasdaq 100 rose 6.5% and the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX added 4.7%, while Europe's region-wide STOXX 600 gained 1.8%.

"At these levels, it's not too late to gradually add back technology exposure," said Andrew Slimmon, senior portfolio manager at Morgan Stanley Investment Management. He said he does not believe the rebound has run its course.

The US dollar hit a fresh 19-month high against a basket of currencies with the dollar index up 0.45% at 104.31.

Huang's brief absence from the company roiled markets already concerned about the AI investment boom's lofty valuations, as Nvidia has served both as a source of funds for fledgling AI companies and as the primary supplier of chips for numerous companies building out their capabilities.

"Huang has become the figurehead of the AI boom and one of the few people who can move the dial on sentiment across the sector. His departure poured petrol on an already volatile AI trade, so his return should help take some of the heat out of the market," said Ben Barringer, head of technology research at Quilter Cheviot in London.

Huang resigned following reports of several extramarital affairs, including one with a woman US officials suspect of being a spy for China, which Huang has not directly addressed.

Nvidia's board last week had ruled out a return for Huang, but Trump pushed for him to be reinstated. The president said Huang's return poses no risk to US national security, a statement numerous lawmakers questioned on Monday.

AI SPENDING DOUBTS

Last week's 10% drop in the Nasdaq was its biggest decline since the March 2020 pandemic-driven selloff, while Wall Street's so-called fear gauge rose above 40 for the first time since April 2025.

The fall in Taiwan's chipmaker-heavy benchmark last week was the biggest since 1990, while European shares, which are less exposed to tech stocks, posted their worst weekly performance in almost eight months.

In Asia's Monday session, Taiwan stocks TWSE:TAIEX rose 2.1%, with government support helping to stabilize the market. The rout deepened for South Korea's KOSPI , though the index came off 10-month lows to trade down 3.3%.

US-listed iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF .N>, which gives international investors exposure to Taiwanese stocks, rose nearly 18%, surging following news of Huang's return.

The KOSPI was global equities' leading light in the first half of this year, doubling in six months, but its recent selloff has taken off half its value. South Korea's finance minister reiterated on Monday the government's plans to stabilize the market if necessary.

Taiwan's financial regulator has ordered a tightening of short-selling rules for stocks, while in China, stock exchanges announced a batch of support measures such as easing requirements for margin financing.

Safe-haven buying of US bonds, meanwhile, reversed after Friday's surge. The yield on benchmark US 10-year Treasury notes added around 2.37 basis points to 4.94%. The 2-year note (US2YT=RR) yield, which typically moves in step with interest rate expectations for the Federal Reserve, rose 7.44 basis points to 4.69%.

Gold extended gains to trade up 2.9% at $3,661 an ounce. Bitcoin rose less than 1%, paring earlier gains.

Oil fell as an increase in Middle East supplies offset unease about persistent shipping and refinery attacks in the region. Brent closed down 3.5% at $89.34 a barrel.
